spec.description: The National Weather Service's Local Storm Reports of the past seven days across the United States, live from NOAA's public ArcGIS service: tornadoes, hail, wind, floods and snow on a map with a time player, density hexbins and a casualties layer, and counts by type and state that follow the map's extent.

options.content:
# Severe weather reports — NOAA / National Weather Service

A replica on this panel of [Esri's ArcGIS dashboard](https://www.arcgis.com/apps/dashboards/94054353efa943b781cc5d6176ca8283),
on the same data and live: the *Local Storm Reports* that the 122 forecast offices of the NWS
publish every day, aggregated by Esri into a public Feature Service.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Source** | `NOAA_storm_reports_v1/FeatureServer/4` — *ALL Storm Reports (past week)*, no token |
| **Pipeline** | Infinity → `f=json` → `latitude`/`longitude`/`time` columns → the panel detects them and kepler draws |
| **Coverage** | rolling 7-day window · one request, no pagination |
| **Licence** | public domain (NOAA); service hosted by Esri |

**Everything beside and below the map is computed for what is on screen** — pan or zoom and the
counts follow. The time player under the map, or a drag across *Reports per day*, narrows them further. `MAGNITUDE` mixes units by type
(inches, knots, EF number), so it is in the tooltip and drives no point size.

params.value: LONGITUDE BETWEEN $west AND $east AND LATITUDE BETWEEN $south AND $north AND INCIDENT_TYPE IN (${type:sqlstring}) AND STATE IN (${state:sqlstring})

spec.description: Reported casualties, summed per day on the server — `CAST(INCIDENT_DATETIME AS DATE)` as the group, so this costs one 300-byte request rather than bucketing 1.951 rows in the browser. **Expect it to be empty most weeks**: casualties appear on roughly 6 reports in 2.000, and a flat zero line here is the true answer, not a broken panel. Follows the map's extent and both pickers; deliberately *not* the player's window, so the brush has a shape to move over. Day buckets are UTC and the finest the service offers.
spec.title: Deaths and injuries per day

body_form.value: LONGITUDE BETWEEN $west AND $east AND LATITUDE BETWEEN $south AND $north
LONGITUDE BETWEEN $west AND $east AND LATITUDE BETWEEN $south AND $north AND INCIDENT_TYPE IN (${type:sqlstring}) AND STATE IN (${state:sqlstring})

spec.description: Reports per UTC day in the map's extent. Grey is every report there; colour is what the type and state pickers leave, by type, in the map's colours. **Drag across the bars** to pick days: the map's time window moves to them, and the counters, the two charts and the table follow. Moving the map's time player moves the brush here, and the eraser in the corner gives back the whole week. The histogram itself does not filter on its window, so there is always the week to pick from. Two server-side group-bys, a few hundred bytes each.
spec.title: Reports per day

params.value: (FATALITIES > 0 OR INJURIES > 0) AND INCIDENT_DATETIME IS NOT NULL

spec.description: Always fetches the whole week. It reads neither the extent variables nor the player's: if it did, zooming out would not bring the rows back — the dataset would no longer hold them. The extent and the brush are masks over data that stays whole.
spec.title: Severe weather reports — last 7 days

body_form.value: HOURS_OLD <= 24 AND LONGITUDE BETWEEN $west AND $east AND LATITUDE BETWEEN $south AND $north AND INCIDENT_TYPE IN (${type:sqlstring}) AND STATE IN (${state:sqlstring})

[{"statisticType":"sum","onStatisticField":"CASE WHEN INCIDENT_TYPE = 'Tornado' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END","outStatisticFieldName":"tornado"},{"statisticType":"sum","onStatisticField":"CASE WHEN INCIDENT_TYPE = 'Hail' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END","outStatisticFieldName":"hail"},{"statisticType":"sum","onStatisticField":"CASE WHEN INCIDENT_TYPE IN ('Wind Damage', 'Wind Gust') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END","outStatisticFieldName":"wind"},{"statisticType":"sum","onStatisticField":"CASE WHEN INCIDENT_TYPE LIKE '%Flood%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END","outStatisticFieldName":"flood"},{"statisticType":"sum","onStatisticField":"CASE WHEN INCIDENT_TYPE = 'Lightning' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END","outStatisticFieldName":"lightning"},{"statisticType":"sum","onStatisticField":"CASE WHEN INCIDENT_TYPE = 'Wildfire' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END","outStatisticFieldName":"wildfire"}]

spec.description: The 24-hour column of the ArcGIS dashboard, in a single request: six `CASE` expressions inside `outStatistics`. A type with no events returns 0 rather than disappearing. Sent as `POST` for the same reason as the block below — with every state picked this query is 1.958 characters as a `GET`, and the ceiling is 2.048.
spec.title: Last 24 hours

body_form.value: INCIDENT_DATETIME BETWEEN COALESCE(NULLIF('$mapFrom', ''), '1970-01-01T00:00:00.000Z') AND COALESCE(NULLIF('$mapTo', ''), '2100-01-01T00:00:00.000Z') AND LONGITUDE BETWEEN $west AND $east AND LATITUDE BETWEEN $south AND $north AND INCIDENT_TYPE IN (${type:sqlstring}) AND STATE IN (${state:sqlstring})

[{"statisticType":"sum","onStatisticField":"CASE WHEN INCIDENT_TYPE = 'Tornado' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END","outStatisticFieldName":"tornado"},{"statisticType":"sum","onStatisticField":"CASE WHEN INCIDENT_TYPE = 'Hail' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END","outStatisticFieldName":"hail"},{"statisticType":"sum","onStatisticField":"CASE WHEN INCIDENT_TYPE IN ('Wind Damage', 'Wind Gust') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END","outStatisticFieldName":"wind"},{"statisticType":"sum","onStatisticField":"CASE WHEN INCIDENT_TYPE LIKE '%Flood%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END","outStatisticFieldName":"flood"},{"statisticType":"sum","onStatisticField":"CASE WHEN INCIDENT_TYPE = 'Lightning' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END","outStatisticFieldName":"lightning"},{"statisticType":"sum","onStatisticField":"CASE WHEN INCIDENT_TYPE = 'Wildfire' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END","outStatisticFieldName":"wildfire"}]

spec.description: The same, for the window the histogram's brush or the map's time player marks (they are one window: `mapFrom` / `mapTo`). With no brush the `mapFrom` / `mapTo` guards span everything and the block shows the whole week. Sent as `POST`: with every state picked and a brush set, the `GET` form is 2.186 characters of query string and Esri answers **404** above 2.048.
spec.title: In the selected days

params.value: LONGITUDE BETWEEN $west AND $east AND LATITUDE BETWEEN $south AND $north AND INCIDENT_DATETIME BETWEEN COALESCE(NULLIF('$mapFrom', ''), '1970-01-01T00:00:00.000Z') AND COALESCE(NULLIF('$mapTo', ''), '2100-01-01T00:00:00.000Z') AND STATE IN (${state:sqlstring})

spec.description: Reports in the map's extent and time window, by event type, in the map's colours. **Click a bar** to filter the whole dashboard by that type; click more bars to add them, click a picked one again to take it out (the last one out means all types). The types not picked stay in grey: this chart does not filter itself. kepler's own filter on `type` writes the same variable, so the map and the chart agree both ways.
spec.title: Reports by type

params.value: LONGITUDE BETWEEN $west AND $east AND LATITUDE BETWEEN $south AND $north AND INCIDENT_DATETIME BETWEEN COALESCE(NULLIF('$mapFrom', ''), '1970-01-01T00:00:00.000Z') AND COALESCE(NULLIF('$mapTo', ''), '2100-01-01T00:00:00.000Z') AND INCIDENT_TYPE IN (${type:sqlstring})

spec.description: The 15 states with most reports in the map's extent and time window, each bar split by event type in the map's colours (the ArcGIS dashboard promises this chart in its *State Chart* title and does not deliver it). **Click a bar** to filter the dashboard by that state; more clicks add states, a picked one clicked again leaves. The states not picked stay, faded.
spec.title: States with most reports

params.value: INCIDENT_DATETIME BETWEEN COALESCE(NULLIF('$mapFrom', ''), '1970-01-01T00:00:00.000Z') AND COALESCE(NULLIF('$mapTo', ''), '2100-01-01T00:00:00.000Z') AND LONGITUDE BETWEEN $west AND $east AND LATITUDE BETWEEN $south AND $north AND INCIDENT_TYPE IN (${type:sqlstring}) AND STATE IN (${state:sqlstring})

spec.description: The list widget of the ArcGIS dashboard. Every row is a link that centres the map on that report: it writes `lat` and `lng`, and the panel's *Center* mapping reads them. Follows the extent, the player's window and both pickers.
spec.title: Most recent reports

options.content:
**Source:** National Weather Service (NOAA) · service aggregated and hosted by Esri ·
[USA Storm Reports](https://www.arcgis.com/home/item.html?id=e109e8fd9c5a495c813b5cbaee9c7d9b)
in the ArcGIS Living Atlas. The reports are **preliminary**; the verified ones live at NOAA's NCEI.

**Deliberate differences from the ArcGIS dashboard.** Its chart is called *State Chart* but groups
by event type; both are here. Its *Rain* indicator queries `INCIDENT_TYPE = 'Heavy Rain'`, a string
that is not in the NWS vocabulary today and therefore always returns 0; *Lightning* and *Wildfire*
take its place. And the time player, the density hexbins, the human-impact layer and the daily
casualty series have no equivalent there.

spec.title: Severe weather reports — NOAA/NWS

spec.description: Filled from the service itself, so the map can never write a value that is not in the list. kepler's filter on `type` and this variable are one state, in two directions.
spec.label: Event type

spec.description: Same as the type: the state chart writes here and the map mirrors it back.
